result:
The proposed answer, 16192/45 (that is, 360·2024/2025 degrees), is probably correct, but I only partly verified it. I did not prove the sufficiency direction.

**Lower bound on α.** The counts must be exactly 0, 1, …, 2024, so some gnome must see all 2024 others. That gnome's view of the others must span at most α.
- A convex hull vertex sees all others within its interior angle. With m hull vertices, the smallest interior angle is at most 180(m−2)/m, which is at most 180·2023/2025.
- For the regular 2025-gon, every vertex has span exactly 180·2023/2025. So α must be at least that value, and the regular polygon is the worst case. This gives inf S = 180·2023/2025, assuming that value itself works.

**Upper end.** Some gnome must also see 0 others. A hull vertex has an exterior gap greater than 180°, which exceeds α for every α < 180. So count 0 is always achievable at a hull vertex, and nothing in the argument rules out values of α close to 180. This gives sup S = 180. This direction relies on a Hall-type argument that the proposed solution only sketches, so it is not rigorously confirmed.

**Small cases.** For n = 3, the equilateral triangle needs α ≥ 60, which matches the formula.

**Sum.** inf S + sup S = 180·2023/2025 + 180 = 180·4048/2025 = 360·2024/2025 = 16192/45.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
